stageA.originalStudentTaskCrossReference: Interpret picture graph symbols, count one category, combine/compare categories, determine which questions are answerable; public source search and source preparation reviewed
stageA.originalWarmup: How Many Do You See? dots within 10, groups of 5, pupil mental explanations
stageA.originalActivity1: Picture-graph comparison including children versus adults sport preferences, count/category facts and explain observations
stageA.originalActivity2: Picture graph of children choosing art supplies; select mathematically answerable questions and explain why motivation/unknown information is not in the graph
stageA.originalSynthesis: Teacher asks how to read title/category labels and graph key before reasoning; student explains why a graph does not supply every requested fact
stageA.publisherCoolDown: Educator-restricted; replaced by independently authored Edulytics question sequence
stageA.visuals: First-party CSS one-symbol pictographs with distinct children/adults and art datasets; publisher visual assets not used

stageB.correctedPedagogy: Read picture graph title, population, key and one symbol per observation; count categories, combine/compare categories; reject questions needing absent motivations or populations
stageB.sourceSafety: 2021 source URL, canonical body SHA, official outcome and prior learner prose required before guarded rewrite

stageC.questionScope: Independent children/adults sport graphs and child art supplies, figure key 1 symbol per response, category counts, addition/compare, and explicit unanswerable why question
stageC.teacherReview: Student mathematical justifications, conversations and picture explanations require teacher rubric not automatic grades
stageC.schoolGradePersistence: Immediate student practice-only feedback; no claim of saved official grade
